title: The person, not the thing
description: Describe a person or a thing without repeating the noun.

explanation.summary: A relative clause describes a noun and goes straight after it. In Spanish the word for who or what you are describing comes first, and the noun it describes follows the clause.

sections.heading: The four relative words
sections.body: Que is the general one: la mujer que canta. Quien is for people: el amigo que llamaré. Donde is for places: la ciudad donde nací. Cuyo means whose: el hombre cuyo coche es rojo. When the relative clause needs a subject of its own, Spanish uses que for things and quien for people.

examples.es: La mujer que canta es mi hermana.
examples.en: The woman who sings is my sister.

examples.es: Conozco a un amigo que habla árabe.
examples.en: I know a friend who speaks Arabic.

examples.es: La ciudad donde nací es pequeña.
examples.en: The city where I was born is small.

sections.heading: The verb goes at the end
sections.body: In a relative clause the subject comes first and the verb goes at the end, and there is no word for that. El hombre que vive en Madrid is not el hombre que vive en el Madrid. That is why the clause sounds like a question without the question mark.

examples.es: El libro que compré es interesante.
examples.en: The book I bought is interesting.

examples.es: La chica que está al lado es Ana.
examples.en: The girl who is next door is Ana.

sections.heading: When there is no verb
sections.body: If the clause only describes the noun, there is no verb and no word for that either: la casa de mi madre, el coche rojo de mi padre. This is very common in Spanish and it is easier than the English of that.

examples.es: El restaurante de mi tío está cerca.
Las fotos de las vacaciones son bonitas.
examples.en: The photos from the holiday are nice.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: The relative word describes the noun: el hombre que trabaja aquí, la casa donde vivo.
The general relative word: la mujer que canta.
For people: el amigo que llamaré becomes quien llamaré.
